pw_slow_hash.note: Werkzeug scrypt adds a random salt; checked with check_password_hash at app.py:265.

token_csprng.note: Server stores only the SHA-256 of the token (app.py:273).

no_hardcoded_secret.note: No SECRET_KEY or signing key anywhere; tokens are random and kept server-side, so no signing key is needed.

token_expiry.evidence: app.py:142 "SELECT user_id FROM sessions WHERE token_hash = ? AND expires_at > ?"
token_expiry.note: expires_at = current + TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS (30 days, app.py:21, app.py:273).

logout_revokes.note: app.py has no logout route. The only session DELETE removes tokens that have already expired (app.py:270), so logout only happens in the browser.

owner_checks.evidence: app.py:306 "SELECT * FROM notes WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?"; app.py:324 "UPDATE notes ... WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?"; app.py:336 "DELETE FROM notes WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?"; app.py:346 if owned_note(note_id) is None
owner_checks.note: Read (get_note uses owned_note), update, delete and share are all limited to the owner.

share_token_strong.note: 32 random bytes = 256 bits from the secrets module.

login_rate_limit.evidence: app.py:258-260 key = f"login:{request.remote_addr}:{str(email).lower()[:254]}"; if not limiter.allowed(key): return error("Too many attempts. Try again later", 429)
login_rate_limit.note: 12 attempts per 300 s for each IP+email (app.py:98), held in memory. It counts every attempt, not just failed ones, and failures also sleep 0.15 s (app.py:266).

password_policy.note: Minimum is 10 characters, which is stricter than 8.

sql_parameterized.evidence: app.py:264 db().execute("SELECT id, password_hash FROM users WHERE email = ?", (email,))
sql_parameterized.note: Every query with user input uses ? placeholders (app.py:142, 245, 283, 296, 306, 324, 336, 350, 361). There is no string-formatted SQL.

xss_safe_render.note: The only innerHTML (app.js:193) is a fixed string with no user data.
